c74object.name: evi_detune
c74object.digest: evieve Gen Object. A quirky digital Detune effect with filtering and saturation
c74object.description:
evi_detune is an abstraction for using inside gen~ or GenExpr.
evi_detune.gendsp requires the GenExpr file(s):
evi_smooth_bank.genexpr, evi_waveshaping.genexpr, evi_crossovers.genexpr, evi_butterworth.genexpr, evi_svfs_tpt.genexpr, evi_adaa.genexpr
evi_detune is also available in MSP as: evi.detune~.
Loosely based on 'mda detune' copyright (c) 1998-2000 Paul Kellett. evi.detune.wrap~ adds a feedback path as would be found in modulation effects, and implements a linkwitz-riley crossover to shift the focus and strength of the effect. In addition a dynamically controllable morphing pre-filter can accentuate certain frequencies hitting the detuner. Feedback path and output are saturated and anti-aliased. See evi.detune~ for a much simpler and efficient version of this algorithm.

geninlet.name: reset
geninlet.digest: Naive. Reset of internal detune phase is naive and not anti-aliased.

attribute.name: crossover
attribute.description: Crossover frequency in Hz. Below this crossover point (the bass) the audio is mono summed, saturated and added back into the wet output mix. Above this crossover point the audio is chanelled through the detune effect.

attribute.name: detune
attribute.description: The main detune parameter. 0 = no detune, 1 = maximum detune. The range is 3 semitones and is converted to table lookup position in samples internally.

attribute.name: drywet
attribute.description: The global dry/wet mix of the detuner. 0 is completely dry, 1 is completely wet.

attribute.name: feedback
attribute.description: The level of gain to send the tapped audio through the feedback saturator.

attribute.name: latency
attribute.description: The amount of time in samples used by the detuner. 0=256, 1=512, 2=1024, 3=2048, 4=4096. This has a strong effect of the granular sound of the effect.

attribute.name: mix
attribute.description: Not dry/wet mix. @mix refers to the internal mix of the wet detune chain. It mixes the crossover low/high audio around the feedback path, thus changing the strength of saturated and unsaturated audio into the detuning effect.

attribute.name: postfilterfrequency
attribute.description: A clean linear lowpass butterworth for attenuating the top end if needed.

attribute.name: prefilterbandwidth
attribute.description: The bandwidth approx 0..10 octaves of the pre-filter (inverse resonance).

attribute.name: prefilterfrequency
attribute.description: The frequency of the pre-filter. A linear TPT morphing filter which can be used for shaping the input to the detuner. Filter type set by @prefiltermorph attribute.

attribute.name: prefiltermorph
attribute.description: Smoothly interpolate the filter type of the pre-filter, 0=lowpass, 0.5=bandpass, 1=highpass.

attribute.name: smooth
attribute.description: Smoothing time of the internal parameters.

attribute.name: window
attribute.description: The gain window to use in the left/right offset of the up/down detuning. 0=flat, 1=Blackman, 2=Exact Blackman, 3=Blackman-Harris, 4=Hann, 5=Hamming. Default Hann.

attribute.name: xover
attribute.description: Crossover frequency in Hz. Below this crossover point (the bass) the audio is mono summed, saturated and added back into the wet output mix. Above this crossover point the audio is chanelled through the detune effect.
